prompt: In a right triangle, angles $A$ and $B$ are the two acute angles. If $\sin A = 0.8$, what is the value of $\cos B$?
hint: The two acute angles of a right triangle are complementary.

hints.text: The two acute angles of a right triangle are complementary.

explanation: The acute angles of a right triangle sum to $90°$, so $B = 90° - A$.
The cofunction identity says $\cos(90° - A) = \sin A$.

alternativeExplanations.title: See it in the triangle
steps: The side opposite angle $A$ is the side *adjacent* to angle $B$ — it is the same physical side.
So $\sin A$ and $\cos B$ are literally the same ratio, over the shared hypotenuse.
That is the whole content of the cofunction identity, and it is a recurring SAT question.
